creator: Chris Huber Reitz
name: English Wikipedia — Writing articles with large language models (content guideline)
quote: The use of large language models (LLMs) to generate or rewrite article content is prohibited except for the uses as outlined below.
quote_label: Wikipedia:Writing articles with large language models (content guideline; RfC March 2026)

provenance.note: Exceptions: copyedits 'after human review' limited to 'spelling, punctuation, capitalisation, grammar, and other simple mistakes' and text must remain 'supported by the sources cited'; translation under WP:LLM-assisted translation. Stated rationale is itself verification economics: LLM text 'can be produced at such a rate that makes review by other editors infeasible' -> partially (per-claim proof is cheap, but review capacity is the scarce resource). No disclosure requirement in this guideline (D3=0). Enforcement: 'Persistent use of large language models outside of the above exceptions is considered disruptive and will result in an editor being blocked from editing.'
